source.title: Selection Principles in Mathematics: A Milestone of Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For a space X, call X a δ-set when every open ω-cover U of X has X in L(U), where L(U) is the closure of U under the operation lim inf applied to sequences of subsets. Call X a γ-set when every open ω-cover contains an infinite subcover in which each point of X belongs to all but finitely many members. Is the δ-property equivalent to the γ-property?

evidence.quote: X is a δ-set (or: has the δ-property) if for each ω -cover U of X, X ∈ L(U). Observe that if {Un}n∈ N is a γ-cover of X, then X = lim inf Un. Thus, the γ-property implies the δ-property. Surprisingly, the converse is still open.
Problem 12.1 ([22, p. 160]) . Is the δ-property equivalent to the γ-property?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, in ZFC, a topological space for which the game G1(D, D) is undetermined, where in inning n player ONE chooses a family U_n of open sets whose union is dense in X, player TWO chooses one set U_n from that family, and TWO wins exactly when the chosen sets still have dense union?

evidence.quote: In the game G1(U, V) ONE chooses in the nth inning an element Un of U and then TWO responds by choosing Un ∈ U n. They play an inning per natural number. A play ... is won by TWO if {Un}n∈ N ∈ V; otherwise ONE wins.
Let D denote the collection of all families U of open sets in X such that ∪U is dense in X.
Problem 13.1 ([8, Question 4.2], [42, footnote 1]) . Does there exist in ZFC a space in which G1(D, D) is undetermined?

accepted.question_text: Let j be the least cardinal κ such that player ONE has a winning strategy in the game G1(K, D) on every Tychonoff space whose cellularity is at least κ, where K consists of open families whose members cover X and D consists of open families with dense union. Is j equal to any standard cardinal characteristic of the continuum?

evidence.quote: Let K denote the families U ∈ D such that {U : U ∈ U } is a cover of X.
Scheepers deﬁnes j as the minimal cardinal κ such that ONE has a winning strategy in G1(K, D) on each Tychonoﬀ space with cellularity at least κ, and shows that cov(M) ≤ j ≤ non(SM Z).
Problem 13.4 ([39, Problem 1]) . Is j equal to any standard cardinal characteristic of the continuum?

accepted.question_text: For a space X, let Σ(Cp(X)) = sup{σ(A) : A ⊆ Cp(X)}, where σ(A) is the least stage at which the iterated sequential-closure process stabilizes. Fremlin proved that Σ(Cp(X)) is always 0, 1, or ω1, and X is called an s1-space when Σ(Cp(X)) = 1. Is the union of fewer than b many s1-spaces again an s1-space?
accepted.context_brief: Closure of s1-spaces under small unions

evidence.quote: Let Σ( X) = sup {σ (A) : A ⊆ X}. Fremlin [16] proved that Σ( Cp(X)) must be 0, 1, or ω 1. If Σ( Cp(X)) = 1 then we say that X is an s1-space.
Problem 15.1 (Fremlin [16, Problem 15(c)]) . Is the union of less than b many s1-spaces an s1-space?

accepted.question_text: Let Cp(X) denote the space of real-valued continuous functions on X with the topology of pointwise convergence. Does Cp(N^N), where N^N is the Baire space, have the Reznichenko (weak Fréchet-Urysohn) property: for every subset A and every point y in the closure of A but not in A, there exists a countably infinite pairwise disjoint family of finite subsets of A such that every neighborhood of y meets all but finitely many members of that family?

evidence.quote: Cp(X) is the subspace of RX consisting of the continuous real-valued functions on X. The topology of Cp(X) is known as the topology of pointwise convergence.

Y satisﬁes the weak Fr´ echet-Urysohnproperty if for each subset A of Y and each element y in A \ A, there exists a countably inﬁnite pairwise disjoint collection F of ﬁnite subsets of A such that for each neighborhood U of y, U ∩ F ̸= ∅ for all but ﬁnitely many F ∈ F . In several works [26, 27, 36] this property appears as the Reznichenko property.
Problem 16.2 ([36, Question 3.6]) . Does Cp(NN) have the Reznicenko property?
This also answers Problem 16.2 in the aﬃrmative.
